home.title: Seventh Steep: gongfu tea timer for puerh and Yunnan white tea

features.title: Grams and temperature
features.text: Pick a tea and a vessel. The app works out the grams of leaf and shows the water temperature in °C or °F.

features.title: Every infusion, on time
features.text: A ring timer runs the rinse and each infusion. A bell and a vibration tell you when to pour.

features.title: Identify a tea from a photo
features.text: Take one to three photos of the tea or its wrapper. The answer is an estimate, not a guarantee.

features.title: Shelf and notes
features.text: Keep a shelf of your teas and write down each session. Your shelf and notes stay on your phone.

home.teas_sub: The app starts from these numbers. You can change the temperature, the vessel and the strength. Tap a tea with a guide to read more.
home.free_p: The timer, the shelf and the notes are free. Every month you get some free photo identifications.
home.plus_p: An optional subscription that gives you more photo identifications. The price and the limits are shown in the app before you buy.
home.private_p: No accounts, no ads, no tracking. Photos go to an AI service only after you agree.
home.langs_note: In English, Ukrainian, Simplified and Traditional Chinese.

shou-puerh-gongfu.title: How to brew shou puerh gongfu style
shou-puerh-gongfu.meta_title: How to brew shou puerh gongfu style: grams, temperature, times
shou-puerh-gongfu.description: Shou (ripe) puerh, gongfu style: {g100} g per 100 ml, {temp_c} °C ({temp_f} °F), a {rinse} s rinse and a full list of infusion times.
shou-puerh-gongfu.card: Ripe, fermented puerh. {temp_c} °C water, a {rinse} second rinse, short first infusions.
intro: Shou, or ripe puerh, is fermented in a wet pile before it is pressed. The taste is dark, smooth and earthy.
It is an easy tea to start with. It takes very hot water and long late infusions. Use the numbers below as a starting point and change them to your taste.
steps: Pour hot water into the empty vessel and the cups to warm them. Pour it out.
Put in {g100} g of leaf for a 100 ml vessel, or {g150} g for 150 ml.
Rinse: fill the vessel, wait {rinse} seconds, pour the water out. Do not drink the rinse.
First infusion: fill the vessel, wait {first} seconds, then pour all of the tea into a pitcher or the cups.
Go on with the next infusion times from the list. Pour out all of the tea each time.
tips: Break a cake or brick into small chunks with a tea pick. Try not to crush the leaf into dust: dust makes a muddy, heavy cup.
Pour out every last drop at the end of each infusion. Leaf that sits in tea keeps brewing and the next cup gets too strong.
Too strong? Make the next infusion a few seconds shorter. Too thin? Make it a few seconds longer.
Bring the water back to the right heat between infusions. Shou likes it close to boiling the whole session.
Keep going while the tea still has taste. After the list, add {step} seconds for each new infusion.

young-sheng-puerh-gongfu.title: How to brew young sheng puerh gongfu style
young-sheng-puerh-gongfu.meta_title: Young sheng puerh gongfu: temperature, grams and steeping times
young-sheng-puerh-gongfu.description: Young sheng (raw) puerh, gongfu style: {g100} g per 100 ml, {temp_c} °C ({temp_f} °F), a {rinse} s rinse and a full list of steeping times.
young-sheng-puerh-gongfu.card: Raw puerh under about five years. {temp_c} °C water, a {rinse} second rinse, fast pours.
intro: Sheng, or raw puerh, is not fermented in a pile. Young sheng (here: under about five years) is bright, floral and fresh, and it can be bitter.
Most of the bitterness comes from water that is too hot or an infusion that is too long. The numbers below keep it in balance. Use them as a starting point and change them to your taste.
steps: Heat the water to {temp_c} °C ({temp_f} °F). The range for this tea is {range_c} °C ({range_f} °F).
Pour hot water into the empty vessel and the cups to warm them. Pour it out.
Put in {g100} g of leaf for a 100 ml vessel, or {g150} g for 150 ml.
Rinse: fill the vessel, wait {rinse} seconds, pour the water out.
First infusion: fill the vessel, wait {first} seconds, then pour all of the tea into a pitcher or the cups.
Go on with the next infusion times from the list. Pour out all of the tea each time.
tips: Pour fast. The first infusions are only {first} seconds, so a slow pour adds a lot of time.
Leave the lid open between infusions. Hot, wet leaf under a closed lid keeps cooking and turns bitter.
Bitter cup? Lower the water by 2 to 3 °C or make the next infusion a few seconds shorter.
Loosen a piece from the cake gently with a tea pick. Whole leaves give a cleaner cup than broken ones.
Keep going while the tea still has taste. After the list, add {step} seconds for each new infusion.
